channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Freezer Festival 2026 — VJ Books
item.description: Freezer Festival Internacional de Fotografía — now in its third edition, curated by photographer and teacher Luciana Demichelis — is looking for photographers and musicians to build a VJ book for its November 2026 programme. A VJ book, also called a bookjockey, is an experimental performance device: a video camera pointed at a table of objects, photographs, fanzines and photobooks, projected live, with a music set played alongside it. The festival has staged three of them so far — Federico Paladino with songs by Seba Rulli at Casa Unclan, curator Luciana Demichelis for the CEF Córdoba visit to the Centro de Arte UNLP, and photographer Amparo Fernández with photographs intervened live. This is the first year it is opened as a call. You can apply as a solo VJ (making the visuals and playing the music set yourself) or as a duo (one on live visuals, one on music). The festival supplies a webcam connected to a projector, a tripod and sound; the application form asks what else you need. Freezer runs from Thursday 5 to Sunday 15 November 2026 across La Plata, Berisso, Ensenada and Buenos Aires, with the Centro de Arte UNLP and the Edificio Karakachoff as its main venues, alongside photographic exhibitions, photobook presentations, open talks, workshops and photographic brigades. Proposals submitted here are also considered for the festival's presentations and curatorial projects through 2027. There is no entry fee. Selected artists are confirmed by email and on the festival's social channels. Applications close 31 October 2026 at 23:59. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Festival exhibition + performance slot.

item.title: Trailhead Gallery 2027 Call for Artists · The Loppet Foundation
item.description: The Loppet Foundation — a Minneapolis non-profit that runs year-round outdoor programming from Theodore Wirth Park under a public/private partnership with the Minneapolis Park and Recreation Board — is booking its 2027 season at the Trailhead Gallery. The gallery sits inside The Trailhead, the Loppet's public building and the trail hub for walkers, skiers, bikers, runners and birdwatchers, so a show there is seen by thousands of park visitors across a four-to-six-week run. Photography is named among the accepted 2D media. The Art Committee gives priority to Minnesota artists whose work speaks to the connection between art and the outdoors, meaningful community connection outdoors, local flora and fauna, inclusion and diversity in the outdoors, sustainability and habitat restoration, wellness, or play. Eligibility as written is 'emerging and established artists in the Twin Cities and surrounding areas', and the Loppet states it strongly encourages BIPOC and Queer-identified artists to apply. Shows are 8–12 pieces, each no larger than 24 x 36 inches and up to 5 lbs, framed or otherwise ready to hang, with one or two larger works possible. Priority consideration goes to submissions emailed between 15 October and 15 November 2026; work sent after 15 November is still accepted and considered on a rolling basis as gallery space allows. This is an unpaid exhibition — there is no fee to apply and no stipend, and artists keep 100% of any sales made directly to buyers. Selection is by the Loppet's Art Committee, a volunteer group of artists, community members, and Minneapolis Park Board and Loppet staff. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Fotografia Calabria Festival Award 2026
item.description: Fifth edition of the award run by the Associazione Pensiero Paesaggio alongside Fotografia Calabria Festival, Calabria's first widespread photography festival (first edition 2022, grown out of the earlier Fiumefreddo Photo Festival). For the first time the competition sets no theme, asking instead for projects with strong conceptual coherence and a recognisable artistic vision; entries are judged on the quality and originality of the photographic research, narrative coherence and the strength of the proposal. Each photographer may enter one project of 10 to 25 images, shot digitally or on film (analogue work scanned), with diptychs allowed; post-production is accepted as an expressive choice, but in documentary projects removing or adding people or objects is not. The winner receives €2,000 in cash from the Festival plus a paid €1,000 commission to publish a project in Internazionale magazine — the two prizes may be combined or awarded separately — along with an exhibition or screening at a forthcoming edition of the Festival and twelve months of promotion. Shortlisted projects go into the permanent online gallery on the Festival's website and its social channels. Copyright stays with the photographer. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: €2,000 + publication in Internazionale + exhibition.

item.title: 53rd Annual Membership Exhibition · Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art
item.description: The Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art's 53rd annual exhibition of work by its own members, on view in the museum's galleries in Saint Joseph, Missouri from 16 January to 21 February 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 15 January from 4 to 7pm and an awards ceremony at 6pm that evening. Photography is category 5 of the ten entry categories, alongside oil and acrylic painting, watercolour, drawing, printmaking, pottery and ceramics, 2-D mixed media, digital art, fibre and textiles, and sculpture and 3-D mixed media; museum staff may reassign a work to the category they think fits. The exhibition is judged, and the entry form carries an opt-out box for artists who do not want their work considered for awards. Entry itself is free, but the show is open only to current AKMA members — new members may join at any time before the drop-off period, with individual membership at $35 a year, $15 for students with a student ID, $20 for teachers and $25 for anyone living more than 60 miles from Saint Joseph. Each individual membership may submit two artworks; a family or dual membership may submit two per person but no more than three as a household. Work must have been made in the last five years, must not have been shown at the museum before, and is capped at 4 by 4 feet including the frame and 50 pounds, with works on paper matted and framed behind glass or Plexiglass and 2-D work wired ready to hang. There is no entry portal: the completed, signed paper entry form is handed in with the artwork at the museum's front desk during the drop-off window of 6 to 10 January 2027, and work is collected again on 22, 23 or 24 February. Artists may mark a work for sale or not; the museum retains 30% on anything sold during the exhibition. Nothing may be removed before the exhibition closes, the museum does not store work, and anything not collected within 30 days is subject to disposal. The Albrecht-Kemper opened as the Albrecht Gallery in 1966 in the former Albrecht family home, took its present name in 1991, and holds one of the Midwest's finest collections of 18th- through 21st-century American art. — Deadline: January 10, 2027. Fee: Free (AKMA membership required, $35/year individual; $15 student). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 41st Annual All-Florida Exhibition · Alliance for the Arts
item.description: The Alliance for the Arts' flagship annual juried show, open to artists living anywhere in Florida and described by the organisation as "the most anticipated of the year" — work from across the 65,000 square miles of the state brought together as a portrait of contemporary Florida art. Photography is one of the named entry categories, alongside painting (oil, acrylic, collage, watercolour, mixed media), drawing, sculpture, ceramics, metalsmithing, glass, digital media, video, printmaking, fibre and textiles. An entry is one to three artworks: $25 for the first, $7 for each additional — though the CaFÉ checkout panel prices the extra works at $5, not $7, so budget for the organiser's higher figure and expect to be charged the platform's. Awards are $1,000 cash for Best in Show, a $300 Blick Art Materials gift certificate for second, $150 cash for third, and a Staff Choice award of a $75 artist membership. Only original work completed in the last two years and not previously shown at the Alliance is eligible; no giclée reproductions. Accepted 2D work must be wired and ready to hang and may not exceed six feet in any direction; 3D work is capped at six feet and 150 lbs. Artists pay their own shipping both ways. Every selected work must be offered for sale to the public at a price the artist sets — entries submitted not for sale are rejected — and the Alliance retains a 40% commission on works sold by non-members, 30% for members. The juror is not yet named. Notification by email on 9 February 2027, accepted work delivered 1 March, and the exhibition runs 5–27 March 2027 in the Alliance's Fort Myers galleries with an opening reception on 5 March. The Alliance for the Arts is a long-running non-profit arts centre on McGregor Boulevard with galleries, a theatre, an art house cinema, an outdoor ArtsPark and a weekly market; it also runs a standing, year-round call for curated-exhibition proposals in all media, photography explicitly among the themes it wants to explore. — Deadline: January 24, 2027. Fee: $25 (1 entry) + $7 each additional. Prize: $1,000 Best in Show + $150 third place.

item.title: No-Type Artist Features — Open Call
item.description: Standing, free open call from No-Type, the independent Chicago photography publisher, for its Artist Features programme. The editors are "looking for new and exciting bodies of work from emerging and established photographers alike", and there are two outcomes: a FEATURE, which is a post carrying the work and the artist statement on No-Type's website and social media, or an INTERVIEW, which is everything in a feature plus a conversation about the artist's practice with editor Dylan Yarbrough. READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING: this call is not the printed magazine. The guidelines are titled "Artist Features" and the licence an applicant grants covers reproduction "on our social media and website as well as for related promotion and archival purposes" — No-Type's themed print issues run as separate, paid calls. There is no cash prize and no exhibition; what is on offer is a curated editorial feature from a publisher whose issues are real printed objects, at no cost to the photographer. Submissions are open on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline, reviewed monthly, and selected artists are contacted directly; the volume of submissions means no individual feedback on work that is not selected. Open to lens-based artists aged 18 and over from any country, emerging or established. Work must be made through a photographic or lens-based process — film, digital capture, archival materials, collage and alternative photographic methods are all named — while AI-generated images or work produced primarily through generative technologies are not eligible. Submit 15 to 20 images as a public link to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or similar, plus a single PDF combining an 80-120 word third-person bio and a 150-250 word statement; JPG, under 10 MB each, 2000 px on the longest side. Multiple submissions are permitted. Artists retain full copyright and are fully credited, and No-Type undertakes not to sell, license or distribute the images for any unrelated purpose without permission. The editors also state they will not edit or alter submitted images, though an image may appear as a cropped detail in a thumbnail or page design. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Online publication feature.

item.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 76: Labour, Repetition and Print
item.description: UK-based independent art zine, edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers, calling for visual art and writing on labour, repetition and print. Print is framed here both as a medium and as a concept — "a mark left through pressure, contact, repetition or reproduction" — so a print can be an impression, a trace, a copy, a record, a pattern, a surface or evidence of an action. The editors want work on repetitive labour and routine; manual, industrial and domestic work; invisible, unpaid and care work; the process of making and skilled labour; printmaking, stamping, copying and seriality; digital reproduction and the circulation of images; and repetition as ritual, habit or compulsion. They ask what it means to make something by hand in an automated, digitally reproduced world, and how repetition might become a strategy for resistance, survival, memory or transformation. ALL MEDIA WELCOME, with photography named explicitly in the list alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, installation, text, film, video, animation, digital art, sound, performance, textile, ceramics, collage and written work; they particularly welcome work that challenges conventional definitions of what constitutes a print, an artwork, or an act of labour. Open internationally to emerging, mid-career and established artists, and explicitly to students, recent graduates and self-taught artists. Free to enter and free if selected. Submit one to three artworks with a statement of up to 300 words explaining how the work connects to the theme; writers may send prose up to 1,000 words or up to three poems. An Instagram handle is a stated requirement — the editors will not select artists without one, because selected work is tagged across their 11,000-follower platform. There is no cash prize: selected works appear in a curated online group exhibition on haus-a-rest.com and across the zine's social channels, typically online for about six months, and artists retain all rights. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: The Landscape: Serene and Savage · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on landscape in both its tranquil and its ferocious registers — gardens, seacoasts and sunsets as readily as thunderstorms, cliffs and floods, with human figures absent, dominant or diminutive. Seascapes, architectural elements, single flowers, trees, birds, animals, reflections and shadows all qualify, in any style from representational to abstract. Photography is one of the accepted media alongside painting, printmaking, sculpture and mixed media, and the gallery sets no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents 18 and over; $35 for three images, $5 for each additional up to nine. An Art of Distinction award gives one artist a special exhibit in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two, a $200 Director's Choice may be granted at the executive director's discretion, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity goes to one artist drawn from everyone exhibited at MVA during the calendar year, and honourable mentions are granted free entry to a future MVA show. Accepted artists ship at their own expense and must enclose a prepaid UPS or FedEx return label, and sales are split 70/30 in the artist's favour. Notification on or about January 26, 2027; exhibition April 4–28, 2027. The jurors have requested anonymity. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition opportunity.

item.title: The Human Family: International Photography Exhibition 2027 · Saturday Review Magazine
item.description: Saturday Review — the magazine founded in 1924 and now being relaunched as a quarterly print journal, with Issue No. 1 due Spring 2027 — is building an international photographic project around one question: what makes us human? Photographers worldwide are invited to submit images about connection, family, work, joy, struggle, ritual, solitude, community, ageing, childhood, culture and identity, documentary or artistic, intimate or expansive. Up to three photographs per €5 entry. Jurying is by Ned Rifkin, the magazine's art editor and former director of the Hirshhorn Museum and Under Secretary for Art at the Smithsonian. One grand prize of €1,000 is awarded and the winning work published in Saturday Review; further selected photographs are published in the magazine and its online gallery. Photographers keep full copyright and grant a non-exclusive licence for the magazine, exhibitions and promotion; book or print-sale use needs a separate agreement. Entries opened 10 October 2026 and close 15 March 2027; results 15 April 2027. — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: €5. Prize: €1,000 + publication.

item.title: Beca Joana Biarnés 2026 · Fundación Photographic Social Vision
item.description: The eighth edition of the grant the Fundación Photographic Social Vision created in 2019 in honour of Joana Biarnés, Spain's first woman photojournalist, who asked before her death that the proceeds of her work be used to strengthen the future of photojournalism. It funds an in-depth photojournalistic investigation carried out inside Spanish territory on a subject of current social relevance. The winner — an individual or a team — receives €8,000 to carry out the work over a maximum of nine months, mentoring throughout from a tutor with extensive teaching and professional experience, the temporary loan of photographic equipment from Foto Ruano Pro, and a guarantee that the finished project will be published in whatever format suits it best. Up to three finalists, the winner included, each get a portfolio review with an expert of their choosing from the foundation's list of collaborators, free access to the narrative-journalism workshop run by the independent magazine 5W and three months of its online subscription. Applicants must be between 18 and 35 years old inclusive and tax-resident in Spain; applications are direct from the author or authors, one proposal each, and in collective projects every member must meet the conditions and one acts as spokesperson. The jury looks for an unpublished subject or a genuinely new perspective on a familiar one, a project still in its early stages with most of the photographic research ahead of it, and work that has not yet received any national or international prize; the outcome must include an extensive series of still photographs, with multimedia accepted only as a complement. Methodology counts: the proposal has to identify expert sources by name, and the funded investigation must include at least two interviews with relevant specialists. The application is entirely free and can be made in Spanish or in Catalan with a Castilian version attached, as a set of PDFs — a CV carrying the ID number, address and date of birth of each participant; a portfolio of at least 25 images of previous work, noting what has already been published; a project presentation with title, justification, motivation in no more than 200 words, methodology and sources, visual approach, and a nine-month schedule and budget; plus a portrait and three photographs of your own connected to the theme, for promotion if you are shortlisted. Everything is sent by WeTransfer or a Dropbox or Drive link, emailed from the applicant's own address. The call runs from 14 September to 16 November 2026. The eighth-edition jury is Bego Antón, Olmo Calvo, Gorka Lejarcegi, María Santoyo and Jordi Rovira. The winner grants the foundation non-exclusive reproduction rights for its own communications and must credit the grant in any publication of the work. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €8,000 + 9-month mentoring + equipment loan.

item.title: HK Photozine & Photobook Dummy Award 2027 · Hong Kong Photobook Festival
item.description: The Hong Kong Photobook Festival's flagship award, open worldwide and free to enter this edition — "The application fee is waived this year" — with only shipping at the applicant's own cost. There are three routes in one call: the Photobook Dummy Award, and the Photozine Award in an Open and a Student category, the latter restricted to full-time students who upload proof of enrolment. The Dummy Award jury shortlists at most 15 finalists, the Photozine Award 10 per category, and three winners are then chosen from each; all finalists' work is exhibited at the Hong Kong Photobook Festival 2027, and the organisers note that previous years' winning and shortlisted dummies have toured to New Zealand, Germany, India, Indonesia, Taiwan, Brazil, Switzerland, Norway and Thailand. Winners get professional exchange with the jury and present their process to the festival audience. The first prize of the Photobook Dummy Award is a subsidy of up to HK$20,000 towards visiting an international photobook festival or self-publishing the book; the Photozine first prize is up to HK$3,000 per category. There is no age or nationality limit. A dummy may be made individually or collectively, must be original, must be self-published or unpublished with no publishing commitment to any registered publisher, may be in any language, needs no ISBN, and must have been created on or after 1 January 2024. A photozine must not exceed 32 pages, must have been created on or after 1 January 2026, and this year's Photozine theme is "Hong Kong". You may apply for both awards but each work may enter only one, and only one entry per award per applicant. Entry is two steps: an online registration form in Chinese or English with a PDF of all pages plus a cover image, then a physical copy with the registration proof in a sealed envelope marked with the award name, which must arrive at the organiser's Wan Chai address by post or in person by 31 January 2027 at 18:00 Hong Kong time — late or incomplete entries are declined. Shortlisted applicants then send a second physical copy within 21 days of the shortlist announcement so the work can tour. Applications opened 1 October 2026; finalists are announced in April 2027 and winners in May 2027. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free (shipping at your cost). Prize: HK$20,000 subsidy + festival exhibition.

item.title: FUTURES Nordic Talents 2027 · Copenhagen Photo Festival
item.description: Copenhagen Photo Festival nominates four Nordic photographers and lens-based artists each year to the FUTURES platform, the European network of photography organisations, and this is the open call for the 2027 cohort. Membership carries an artist fee of €500 and access to online conversations with experts, tutoring sessions, the annual FUTURES platform event, events hosted by the network's other member organisations and FUTURES meet-ups, plus continuous promotion on the platform's website, social media and print material; members can also enter two open calls exclusive to FUTURES artists, one for a travelling exhibition that moves between partnering venues across the year and one for an annual exhibition. On top of that the festival gives the nominated artists a screening of their submitted work during Copenhagen Photo Festival 2027, publication in the FUTURES archive on the CPF site, promotion on CPF's channels, free entry to the 2027 festival, an invitation to the festival's networking days and a portfolio session with Maja Dyrehauge Gregersen. Three eligibility conditions all have to hold: you have been resident in Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway or Sweden for at least the past 12 months; you were born in 1988 or later; and you have either studied photography or art, or your CV shows continual professional experience over the last three years, such as taking part in an exhibition or a publication. Applicants who entered previous FUTURES open calls may apply again unless they were previously selected as platform members. The application is a single PDF of at most 10 MB — CV and bio on no more than two pages, a project description on no more than one page, and 10 to 20 photographs from your latest or current project — submitted through the festival's own form with a DKK 100 administrative fee. The organisers ask for a cohesive photography or art project with a conceptual background that relates to your wider practice, ongoing or new. The festival's Programme Committee, whose members work in curation, publishing and visual storytelling, makes the selection; applicants hear back in mid-December 2026 and the four talents are announced in February 2027, ahead of the November 2027 festival. Previous CPF nominees include Emma Sarpaniemi, Inuuteq Storch, Jenni Toivonen and María Kristín Antonsdóttir. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: DKK 100. Prize: €500 + FUTURES platform membership + CPF 2027 screening.

item.title: ART WEIRD AND WILD · MVA Gallery
item.description: A national call from the MVA Gallery in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania for the strange and the unconventional: "If your art is strange or unconventional, this is the exhibition for you. Please share your weird and wild images with the Gallery's art enthusiasts and collectors." The gallery places the show in the lineage of Surrealism, Dadaism, Expressionism, Metaphysical Painting and Magic Realism, and offers a long but open list of directions — dreams, nightmares and the unconscious; enigmatic landscapes; mysterious and supernatural scenes; bizarre creatures; eerie light and shadow; distortion and fragmentation; unexpected colour combinations; visual narratives of alienation, anger and psychological distress; subverted perspective; personal references to memory, eroticism and childhood; surprising juxtaposition of objects; metamorphosis of people, animals and objects — "and anything else -- ordinary or eccentric, subtle or dramatic -- that excites you. You have limitless creative freedom for this exhibition." Photography is a named medium and the prospectus is unusually welcoming about process and presentation: "All photographic processes are welcome", with framing in black or white preferred for a traditional presentation, white or off-white mats, and unframed mounting considered. There is no cutoff date for when the work was made, and work previously shown at MVA is not eligible. A small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers, curators and academics juries the entries and has requested anonymity for this show; decisions are final and no feedback is given. Awards are an "Art of Distinction" award — a featured solo presentation in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date — a $200 Director's Choice award at the Executive Director's discretion, honourable mentions that carry free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity chosen in December from everyone exhibited that calendar year. The exhibition runs 4–28 April 2027; artists are notified on or about 23 February 2027 and accepted work must reach the gallery by 31 March. Work has to arrive ready to hang with stretched wire on the back, under 48 inches framed and 45 lbs, plexiglass preferred over glass; sculpture is capped at 28 inches in any dimension. Artists pay shipping and insurance both ways and must enclose a prepaid return label. The gallery keeps 30% on sales. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Nikon Fotobus Grant 2026
item.description: A project-continuation grant for emerging photographers from Fotobus e.V., the Hannover-based photography society, funded with Nikon. Three awards are made — €5,000, €3,000 and €2,000 — and each of the three funded projects also receives a Nikon camera, with the full sum paid out immediately on announcement and no restrictions on how it is spent. What is funded is the continuation of a photographic project already under way: all genres of photography are welcome, group applications from two or more photographers are allowed, and the work may use text, found images, documents or drawings alongside the photographs as long as its core is photographic. Video works are not accepted and AI-generated images are excluded outright — the society funds photography only — while manipulation and staging are permitted in conceptual work provided they are disclosed in the captions; applicants also accept the World Press Photo Code of Ethics. Eligibility runs on either of two alternatives, with nationality irrelevant to both: being enrolled as a student at a university in Germany, Austria or Switzerland at the time of applying (no age limit, and any subject, not only photography), or being no older than 30 and resident in Germany, Austria or Switzerland. Membership of Fotobus is not required. One application per person, though you may additionally join a group application, and an unfunded project may be entered again next year. The application is free and goes only through Picter: a project description of up to 3,000 characters answering the organisers' set questions, a maximum of 30 images from the unfinished project, and a CV of up to 1,500 characters — the quality of the edit and the sequence are explicitly part of the jury's assessment. The jury meets in mid-November, a shortlist of 20 is published on 1 December 2026 and the three funded projects on 15 December 2026, with the one-year funding period running to 15 December 2027 and a final report due at the end of it. NOTE ON THE CLOSING DATE: the organiser's own page advertises 1 November 2026 at 23:59 German time, but the Picter form that applications must go through is set to close on 31 October at 23:59 German time — treat 31 October as the operative date. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 / €3,000 / €2,000 + Nikon camera.

item.title: VI Premio Editorial de Fotografía Documental Galega · FFoco Festival
item.description: The sixth edition of the Galician Documentary Photography Publishing Prize, run by the non-profit Asociación Recreativo Cultural Acolá — the association behind FFoco, the A Coruña photography festival, which marks its tenth edition at the Fundación Luis Seoane between October and December 2026 — and financed in full by the Fundación Marta Ortega Pérez. The prize exists to turn a documentary project into a book: entrants are not expected to arrive with a finished, print-ready dummy, and the organisers describe the call as accompanying a project until it acquires new value in book form. Open to photographers and collectives whose work is connected to Galicia, satisfying at least one of three conditions — born in Galicia, resident in Galicia, or presenting a project centred on or thematically and conceptually linked to Galicia. Subject matter is free, but the work must be documentary, original and previously unpublished in book form with no edition committed to a third party; earlier showing in exhibitions, magazines, digital publications or social media does not disqualify a project as long as the author still holds the rights needed to publish it as a book. Entry is a single PDF of at most 20 MB containing an essay or maquette of 30 to 60 photographs, plus a project description and a biography of up to 300 words each. An independent jury of publishing professionals and representatives of established imprints picks up to eight finalists and then one winner, judging technical quality, originality, narrative capacity, coherence and editorial viability; the jury's composition is published with the result and its decision is final. The winning project is published by the Galician imprint Alauda Negra with Acolá covering every editorial and production cost — image editing and selection, editorial direction and design, layout, pre-press, paper, printing and distribution — and the winner also receives €1,000 for the publishing rights under an editorial contract. Non-winning projects keep all their rights. The five previous winners are Ana Paes, Ana Núñez Rodríguez, the Cadela Negra collective, Iván Nespereira and Jesús García. Submissions close Sunday 18 October 2026 at 23:59 peninsular Spanish time. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Photobook published by Alauda Negra + €1,000.

item.title: Open Call Pop-up-Galerien Herbst 2027 — Waldviertel/Industrieviertel · Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich
item.description: Free open call, no entry fee, for the two pop-up galleries Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich runs in Bad Fischau-Brunn (Industrieviertel) and Horn (Waldviertel). In the second half of 2027 each gallery gives three artists a four-week exhibition — six slots in all — with the exact periods still to be announced ("Im zweiten Halbjahr 2027 bieten beide Galerien jeweils drei Künstlerinnen bzw. Künstlern die Möglichkeit zu einer vierwöchigen Ausstellung"). The 2027 edition keeps the existing free exhibition offer for members — "Das kostenlose Ausstellungsangebot für Mitglieder bleibt bestehen" — and adds a sharper focus on the artists themselves: "Neu ist der stärkere Fokus auf die Künstlerinnen und Künstler, ihre Arbeitsweisen und die mediale Begleitung der Ausstellungen." WHAT THEY WANT: "Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Persönlichkeiten hinter den Arbeiten" — the people behind the work, their artistic positions and personal approaches made visible. The gallery room can be drawn deliberately into the exhibition concept, and an idea for a mediation format the artist can run independently is a required part of the submission. NO MEDIUM IS NAMED AND NONE IS EXCLUDED: the call addresses "Künstlerinnen und Künstler sowie Kunsthandwerkerinnen und Kunsthandwerker" — artists as well as craftspeople — so a photographic project competes on the same terms as any other, and the Horn gallery's own 2026 programme included Fotoclub VHS Horn; what is being judged is an exhibition concept for a specific room, not a set of images. WHO CAN APPLY: artists from the Industrieviertel for the Bad Fischau-Brunn gallery and from the Waldviertel for Horn — each region is tied to one venue — and membership of Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich is a condition of entry ("Mitgliedschaft bei der Kulturvernetzung Niederösterreich erforderlich"), €25 a year for artists and individuals on the organisation's own membership form. WHAT A SELECTED ARTIST GETS: the exhibition space free of charge, support with press and public relations, and professional atelier and portrait photographs plus a short video about their way of working, played in the gallery through the exhibition and given to the artist afterwards. WHAT IS ASKED IN RETURN is more than hanging work: the artist installs and dismantles the show themselves ("Selbstständiger Auf- und Abbau der Ausstellung") and organises both the vernissage and the finissage, with compulsory attendance on those two weekends at set hours — Saturday and Sunday 17:00–19:00 in Bad Fischau-Brunn, Saturday 17:00–19:00 and Sunday 15:00–17:00 in Horn — plus coordination with Kulturvernetzung, taking part in the video and photos, and promotion through the artist's own network. A further event, such as an artist talk, workshop or guided tour, is "erwünscht, aber keine Voraussetzung". SUBMIT: one PDF of no more than 8 MB with contact details, an exhibition concept with images running to at most two A4 pages, portfolio and CV, and the mediation-format idea, by email to the separate address published for each region. Selection is notified in early 2027; neither the listing nor the call's own PDF names a jury. — Deadline: November 19, 2026. Fee: Free (Kulturvernetzung NÖ membership required, €25/year individual). Prize: Four-week exhibition + atelier video and professional photos.

item.title: Kala Yatra International Artist Residency 2026/27
item.description: Year-round residency in the Kathmandu valley with Kala Yatra (कला यात्रा, “Art Journey”), an artist-run not-for-profit collective that curates concept-based exhibitions, socially relevant projects and residencies alongside workshops and educational outreach. The collective says residents “will benefit from a supportive art community and valuable resources” and that it prioritises “not only your artistic endeavors but also the relationships and collaborations that may emerge”, with the chance to explore Nepal's contemporary art scene, cultural diversity and geography. The residency offers networking opportunities and presentations at Kala Yatra and partner institutions, and says it can facilitate exhibitions or help residents navigate galleries and studios. Accommodation is an individual bedroom with linens, private or shared bathroom depending on the booking, a shared kitchen, a common working space, solar hot water, wi-fi (bring your own laptop), weekly housekeeping and a digital guidebook; airport pick-up and drop-off are available at extra cost. THE ARTIST PAYS: “We run an artist-led, self-funded residency and currently have no available funding. To cover administrative and utility expenses, we charge a minimal fee based on the duration of your stay” - €200 for two weeks, €400 for a month, and a reduced €300 a month for artists who are both residents and citizens of the SAARC countries (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka). There is no application fee and applications are accepted all year, by email: artist statement, CV or bio with a portfolio or website link, up to ten recent works in a single PDF, a copy of a valid passport and the collective's application form. Stays start at a minimum of two weeks and the collective asks artists to apply at least three months ahead because slots fill; the residency fee covers none of the airfare, visa fees, health insurance, local transport, food, materials or project costs, and airport pick-up is €25 on pre-booking. The programme is “open to, but not limited to” visual artists, painters, sculptors, ceramists, printmakers, performing artists, musicians, writers, new media artists, curators, filmmakers, theatre artists, architects, art critics and researchers, and invites anyone whose practice is not on that list to write in; a current resident is credited on the residency's own page as a “Visual Artist, Writer & Photographer”. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: €200 (2 weeks) / €400 per month (€300 per month for SAARC artists). Prize: Residency.

item.title: SÍM Residency — January–March 2027
item.description: Open call for one- to three-month residency stays in January, February and March 2027 at the SÍM Residency in Reykjavík, run by SÍM – the Association of Icelandic Visual Artists. The programme describes itself as “one of the Nordic region's most established artist residency programmes, welcoming around 200 artists and cultural practitioners from around the world each year”, and it offers private and shared studios, accommodation, an orientation meeting, an artist page on the residency's own website and social channels, and opportunities for public presentations and artist talks. It is open to “all creators and art practitioners” working in “all mediums of visual arts, design, architecture, music, dance, performance art, creative writing, curation, cultural work, and scientific research”; photographers are among the residents the programme publishes, including projects built by “repeatedly assembling, photographing, dismantling, and reassembling” found Icelandic materials and a multidisciplinary body of work made “through painting, photography, and printmaking”. THE ARTIST PAYS: SÍM is a nonprofit, self-funded programme with only partial facility support from the City of Reykjavík, so applying is free but a selected artist owes a 50,000 ISK non-refundable programme fee within 15 days of acceptance plus a monthly accommodation fee of 140,000 ISK for a single bedroom-studio and 210,000-280,000 ISK for a twin - the first month payable two months before arrival, also non-refundable. BUDGET THE HIGHER FIGURE: the page prints its room prices twice and the two tables disagree on two of the twins - the application form's own room selector charges 240,000 ISK for bedroom 18 and for bedroom-studio 2, where the Residency Fees block lists them at 210,000 and 230,000 - so one month in the cheapest room costs at least 190,000 ISK all in. The fee covers administration, a SÍM membership card, wi-fi, parking, bedding and towels, communal kitchen equipment, laundry, heating, water and electricity and basic tools in the project space; meals, materials, insurance, travel, living costs and workshop fees are not included, and the fee “does not constitute rent” so a resident does not become a tenant. Applicants must hold at least a BA, though “exceptions may be made for self-taught artists who demonstrate high professionalism in their artistic practices, supported by a compelling CV and project proposal”. The application asks for a 400-word project description covering the conceptual framework, research questions and working methods, three images of previous work (10MB total) and a CV; proposals touching sustainability, ecology, global warming, geology, the environment, Icelandic culture or Nordic language are flagged as an advantage. January and February applications are reviewed as they arrive with a reply within two weeks, and the residency notes a vibrant shared-living environment with communal kitchens that may not suit everyone. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free to apply; ISK 50,000 programme fee + ISK 140,000–280,000/month accommodation if accepted. Prize: Residency.

item.title: ICP Curatorial Vision Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: A $10,000 scholarship from the International Center of Photography for one emerging curator, covering most of the $12,500 tuition for ICP's Online One-Year Certificate in Curatorial Practice in Photography. The award “supports an emerging curator in developing the critical perspectives, research, and curatorial approaches needed to engage with photography and visual culture today”, and ICP frames it as “contributing to a more diverse and expansive conversation around the photographic image”. One recipient is chosen on the strength of the application materials and portfolio, and finalists may be invited to a Zoom interview. Both the programme application (through SlideRoom, $60 fee) and the separate scholarship application must be submitted by 18 October 2026, so a recipient's remaining cost is $2,500 of tuition plus that application fee. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in ICP's One-Year Certificate programmes - part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible - and awards cannot be combined, so an applicant may receive only one. ICP encourages applicants to apply for every scholarship they are eligible for. Decisions arrive by email with the admission letter; ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: $10,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: ICP Image Text Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: A $10,000 scholarship from the International Center of Photography for one emerging writer, artist or image-maker working at the intersection of photography and language, covering most of the $12,500 tuition for ICP's Online One-Year Certificate in Writing and the Photographic Image. ICP describes it as supporting “emerging writers, artists, and image-makers in developing their critical voice at the intersection of photography and language”, with the aim of fostering “new perspectives on photography and its role in shaping how we understand and engage with the world”. One recipient is chosen on the strength of the application materials and portfolio, and finalists may be invited to a Zoom interview. Both the programme application (through SlideRoom, $60 fee) and the separate scholarship application must be submitted by 18 October 2026, leaving a recipient $2,500 of tuition plus that fee. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in ICP's One-Year Certificate programmes - part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible - and awards cannot be combined, so an applicant may receive only one. ICP encourages applicants to apply for every scholarship they are eligible for. Decisions arrive by email with the admission letter; ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: $10,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: ICP Latin Vistas Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: Up to ten $5,000 scholarships from the International Center of Photography for emerging curators, writers, photographers and image-makers from Latin America, applied against the $12,500 tuition of any of ICP's three Online One-Year Certificate programmes - Curatorial Practice in Photography, Writing and the Photographic Image, or Documentary Practice: Visual Storytelling. ICP describes the award as supporting applicants “committed to exploring new perspectives through photography and visual storytelling”, giving recipients “the opportunity to develop their practice, expand their critical and creative approaches, and engage with ICP's international community of image-makers”. It is open to applicants who are from and currently reside in Latin America. Recipients are chosen on the strength of the application materials and portfolio, and finalists may be invited to a Zoom interview. Both the programme application (through SlideRoom, $60 fee) and the separate scholarship application must be submitted by 18 October 2026; the $5,000 covers part of the tuition, so a recipient still pays the $7,500 balance plus the application fee. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in the One-Year Certificate programmes - part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible - and awards cannot be combined, so an applicant may receive only one, though ICP encourages applying for every scholarship for which you are eligible. Decisions arrive by email with the admission letter; ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: Up to 10 × $5,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: TOTALLY OPEN · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest, the artist-run 501(c)(3) creative research gallery in Cincinnati, reverses its own method for a third year running: instead of naming a theme and calling for work about it, it opens the call to anything and discovers the theme (or themes) afterwards, through the curatorial process. "Utilizing a reduced entry fee to lower certain barriers to access, this call is TOTALLY OPEN - completely open to any work, any media, and idea, under the umbrella of 'visual art'." Open to everyone internationally - "There is no limitation to this special call" - although artists living in Ohio, Kentucky and Indiana are pointed to the Regional Showcase that shares this exhibition slot. Selection is two-part: an anonymous several-member panel of professional and academic advisors with a broad range of expertise scores the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibit curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium with no strings attached, and one work in each of the season's nine exhibition periods takes a $1,000 Grand Jury Award, decided by a second-round jury of the top-scoring works - a process that "applies to all exhibitions during our 23rd season, beginning September 25, 2026, and continuing through August 2027, including this one". The exhibition runs 5 March - 2 April 2027; notifications are emailed to all entrants by 25 January 2027 and accepted work is due at the gallery by 27 February. There is no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery's door, no restriction on when the work was made, and no requirement that work be for sale - the gallery keeps 30% on anything sold and artists pay shipping both ways. Manifest runs its own darkroom and photo lab and publishes the INPHA photography annual, so photographic work sits squarely inside this call. The entry form takes up to twelve works at $10 each, paid by credit card via PayPal on the page that follows the form, or by US check or money order. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $10 per work. Prize: $50 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury.

item.title: Regional Showcase: Ohio, Kentucky & Indiana · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest's annual exhibit devoted to artists living in its own three-state region, a series the Cincinnati gallery launched thirteen years ago. "It is VERY important to note that this is NOT a call for works ABOUT Ohio, Kentucky, or Indiana. There is no thematic or media requirement. The exhibit is solely focused on works by artists living in the three states, to celebrate the diversity and quality of the artwork made by people in our region." The only limitation is residence: entries must be original works made by artists currently living in Ohio, Kentucky or Indiana. Submissions "can range from the most traditional to the most conceptual or experimental", across any 2D, 3D or experimental medium, with no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery's door and no restriction on when the work was made - Manifest states it does "not believe great art has an expiration date". Selection is two-part: an anonymous several-member panel of professional and academic advisors scores the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibit curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium with no strings attached, and one work in each of the season's nine exhibition periods takes a $1,000 Grand Jury Award decided by a second-round jury of the top-scoring works. The exhibition runs 5 March - 2 April 2027; notifications are emailed to all entrants by 25 January 2027 and accepted work is due at the gallery by 27 February. Manifest is a 501(c)(3) run by artists for artists, with its own darkroom and photo lab and an international photography annual, and it notes that the entry fee "is the only cost charged by Manifest for participation" - though artists pay shipping both ways and the gallery keeps 30% on work that sells. The entry form takes up to twelve works: $45 covers the first three, then $5 each. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 works) + $5 each. Prize: $50 honorarium + $1,000 Grand Jury.

item.title: Juried Artist Membership 2026 · Rockport Art Association & Museum
item.description: Once a year the Rockport Art Association & Museum - founded in 1921 on Cape Ann, with galleries at 12 Main Street - juries new Juried Artist Members, and Photography is one of its four standing categories alongside Painting, Graphics and Sculpture. Admission is by merit: "Juried Artist Members ... are admitted through an annual jury process in the fall that evaluates the merit of their work based on professionalism of technique and originality." Applicants submit five original works in one category, created solely by the applicant - no work made in classes or under supervision - framed or presented to a professional standard, and the actual physical works must be delivered to the museum for the jury to see (drop-off Tuesday 27 October, pick-up Thursday 29 October). Photographs may not be printed smaller than 11 by 14 inches and frames may not exceed 20 by 24 inches at the opening. The jury votes silently and a photography applicant needs at least four of five votes in favour; works that split 60/40 are reviewed a second time, when a juror may speak for or against. No feedback is given. The RAA&M states there is no longer a New England residency requirement to apply. Accepted artists have about two works chosen for the New Juried Artist Members Show, 7-29 November 2026, with a reception on 7 November, and membership then brings "exhibition opportunities in solo, member group, non-juried & juried shows; opportunities to instruct and attend workshops; and participation in year-round classes, sketch groups, lectures and artist demonstrations". The application fee is $50 whatever the category - you may apply in more than one category on a single fee, but must submit five works per category - and it is deducted from the $150 annual dues if you are accepted. The association insures nothing: "The RAA&M does not offer insurance on works submitted by applicants." — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: $50 ($150 dues if accepted). Prize: Juried artist membership + group exhibition.

item.title: Earth Photo 2027
item.description: Earth Photo is the free international platform for photographers and filmmakers who work on the natural world, its peoples and environments: "From the effects of climate change and biodiversity loss to powerful acts of restoration, resilience and hope, Earth Photo sheds light on the stories behind the images." Established in 2018 by Parker Harris with the Royal Geographical Society and Forestry England, and organised in partnership with Photoworks, it is open to artists and image-makers worldwide working in any lens-based media. Each entrant may submit up to ten works, still or moving - short films between five seconds and five minutes - with a CV up to 500 words, a 100-word artist statement and a caption or statement for each work. Work should have been made in the last five years, though earlier images may be included as part of a long-term documentary project, archive or vernacular series. The Earth Photo team longlists the most compelling submissions for a jury of industry experts chaired by Louise Fedotov-Clements, Director of Photoworks, with the shortlist then considered for exhibition and awards; final decisions rest with the Earth Photo team and its exhibition and award partners. The awards are substantial and various: the Earth Photo Award 2027 (£1,000), the Climate of Change Award (£500), the Moving Image Award (£500), a two-week Sidney Nolan Trust residency at The Rodd with access to Nolan's photographic archives for a UK-based practitioner, two David Wolf Kaye Future Potential Awards of £1,000 plus mentoring for practitioners aged 25 or under, a £400 Photoworks digital residency, mentoring from the New Scientist editorial team with a possible feature in its Aperture section, and a QUAD feature exhibition. Shortlisted and winning work opens at the Royal Geographical Society in London on 5 July 2027 and then tours UK venues - the 2026 edition travelled to National Trust properties, Belvoir Castle, Chester Zoo, Heligan Gardens and Castle Ward among others - with publication in the RGS magazine Geographical and RGS membership for the award winners. The cutoff is not end of day: the KEY DATES block reads "Online submission deadline 3 February 2027, 5pm GMT". Entrants are notified on 11 March 2027; high-res files are due 25 March. — Deadline: February 3, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 + exhibitions + residency.

item.title: GOING GREEN · MVA Gallery
item.description: A national call from the MVA Gallery in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, built entirely around one colour: "Green is located in the center of the color spectrum as if to proclaim its significance as the center of the color universe!" The gallery asks how you use it - "Does the color permeate your entire image or is it used in small sections? Does it appear in your artwork in objects or in nature or in portrait studies or in abstract design? Is Green purely decorative, or is it a narrative or structural device?" - and sets no other limit: "No restrictions on subject matter or style exist for this exhibition. All approaches are acceptable - traditional or experimental, representational or abstract, unified or fragmented, lucid or mysterious." Photography is a named medium and the prospectus is unusually welcoming about process and presentation: "All photographic processes are welcome", with framing in black or white preferred for a traditional presentation, white or off-white mats, and unframed mounting considered. There is no cutoff date for when the work was made. A small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers, curators and academics juries the entries and has requested anonymity for this show; decisions are final and no feedback is given. Awards are an "Art of Distinction" award - a featured solo presentation in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date - a $200 Director's Choice award at the Executive Director's discretion, honourable mentions that carry free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity chosen in December from everyone exhibited that calendar year. The exhibition runs 4-28 April 2027; artists are notified on or about 11 February 2027 and accepted work must reach the gallery by 31 March. Work has to arrive ready to hang with stretched wire on the back, under 48 inches framed and 45 lbs, plexiglass preferred over glass; artists pay shipping and insurance both ways and must enclose a prepaid return label. The gallery keeps 30% on sales. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: BBA One Shot Award - Winter 2027
item.description: BBA Gallery's single-image prize, the Berlin gallery's most accessible open call: "We are looking for that one definitive frame that stops viewers in their tracks." One photograph, one €19 entry, and the gallery's own summary of the rules is "1 shot - 0 rules (almost)" - "You do not need a massive portfolio or an expensive series to make an impact in the art world", "We welcome artists of any background, nationality, and ability, our only rule is that you must be over 18 to apply", and "You can submit work in absolutely any photographic medium or genre." A shortlist of 20 images is professionally printed and hung at BBA Gallery with all production costs covered by the gallery, and a longlist of 50 is shown on a large digital display in the space; there is no shipping cost to the artist. First prize is €300 in cash plus the exhibition, an Artsy profile and promotion through the gallery's social channels and newsletter, and selected images are also featured weekly online as Shot of the Week. BBA runs these prizes as an entry point into its gallery programme rather than as a one-off: "We built these open calls not just to hand out titles, but to foster real connections between emerging talent and the established art world", and it says prize artists go on to its Berlin events, group shows, art-fair representation and solo exhibitions. Previous One Shot winners include Michael Bulgrin (Germany), Rik Roos and Peter Alfred Hamelinck (Netherlands), Pervin Donmez (Latvia) and Calogero Cammalleri (Italy). Two conditions sit in the terms rather than the pitch: submitted work "must be available exclusive for sale throughout the exhibition and three months after if sales are made through BBA Gallery", and the gallery takes 50% commission on anything it sells. Entry is one .jpg, .png or .heic file up to 3 MB, uploaded after the fee is paid. — Deadline: February 22, 2027. Fee: €19. Prize: €300 + Berlin exhibition.

item.title: smallworks 2026
item.description: ROY G BIV's annual small-format holiday show, open to the Columbus nonprofit's own Artist and ROY Alumni members. Every piece must fit inside a 12 x 12 x 12 inch envelope — two-dimensional work included, so photography and lens-based work qualify as long as it arrives ready to hang with the right hardware. You can submit up to five entries and the gallery guarantees each member at least one accepted work, with a maximum of three, which makes this one of the rare juried shows where entering is close to a certainty of being hung. The gallery asks artists to price work 'in the spirit of the season of giving' and splits any sale 65% to the artist, 35% to ROY. Submission is by email with the subject 'smallworks 2026': attach high-quality JPEG or PNG images named only with a number, each no larger than 1.5 MB and never zipped, plus a list of works giving title, date, media, size and price; submissions missing the artist's full name, mailing address, attached images or attached list of works will not be considered. Artists are notified of admittance on Sunday November 15, accepted work is delivered to the gallery at 435 West Rich Street on Saturday November 28 and Sunday November 29 between 12:30 and 5:30pm EST, and the artist is responsible for transport both ways. The gallery states on its mission page that the price of work shown at ROY includes its 35% commission, reinvested in the gallery. ROY G BIV has run for 37 years and given over 1,000 emerging artists their exhibiting opportunity; its alumni hold work in permanent collections at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Whitney, MoMA PS1, the Louvre, the Getty, Tate Modern and the Columbus Museum of Art, and hold "64 major awards (that we know of), including 2 Guggenheim Fellows". Membership in the Artist or Alumni tier is the only cost, taken through the gallery's Donorbox form, which publishes no fixed price. — Deadline: November 8, 2026. Fee: PWYC. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Best of the Beach
item.description: A juried show at Gallery of Hermosa on Pier Avenue in Hermosa Beach, presented with the local Easy Reader newspaper, and the gallery is blunt that this is not a beach-art show: 'Artistic excellence is the standard, and there is no required subject. Subject matter, style, and medium are open.' The title is meant as an invitation rather than a theme — submit the work you believe is your best and say why it belongs. A short artist statement of up to 100 words is strongly recommended with each entry, and the gallery offers several readings to work from: your strongest piece, the beach as literal subject (coastline, water, light, wildlife, surf culture, life by the sea), the beach as metaphor (shoreline, tide, horizon, edge, impermanence, the meeting of two worlds), a personal connection to a place or community, or your own take. Open to local, national and international artists in any medium: 2D work in all media plus smaller 3D sculpture. Best in Show takes $500 and an article in Easy Reader, whose length, format and timing the paper decides; second place takes $200, third $100, and four further awards $50 each, announced at the opening reception, where winners need not be present. Entry is $36 for up to three images, with detail shots counting toward that total, and the jury's decision does not guarantee acceptance. Decisions are emailed November 30, accepted work is dropped off December 7–9, the reception runs Saturday December 12 from 2 to 5pm, and the exhibition hangs December 12, 2026 to January 10, 2027, with pick-up on January 11–12. All accepted work must be offered for sale, at the gallery and online, from the time of acceptance — work marked not for sale is not eligible — and neither the gallery nor the CaFE prospectus states a commission on a sale. The artist is responsible for delivering or shipping work to and from the gallery. Two-dimensional work may be up to 48 inches wide by 72 inches high including the frame and 25 lbs, must arrive ready to hang on braided picture wire (no sawtooth hangers), and anything over 20 inches on a side must be glazed with acrylic rather than glass; photographs must be framed or mounted on board, and must be unique or part of a limited edition, with the series and edition noted on the work. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $36 for up to 3 images. Prize: $500 + Easy Reader article / $200 / $100 + 4×$50.

item.title: THROWING SHADE · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's online juried exhibit on light and shadow — the organisers write that the two 'speak to the parts of us that words miss', light revealing and shadow concealing, and that in the space between them mystery and emotion come alive. They want your version of that in any medium. Open worldwide to amateur and professional artists in all fine art media, with photography named explicitly in the list alongside oil, acrylic, watermedia, pastel, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, fiber, wood, ceramics, film/video and digital art; AI will not be accepted, work previously selected for an Art Fluent exhibit is not eligible, and neither is work copied or made under an instructor's guidance. Curated and juried by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill with an anonymous committee of jurors — there is no personal feedback. Best of Show takes $750 and two Director's Choice awards take $250 each; every accepted piece is shown in the online gallery at art-fluent.com, sales enquiries go straight to the artist and the artist keeps 100% of any sale. JPEGs are due by midnight MST on Friday, January 8, 2027, with notification and the online gallery opening by February 5. Entry is $25 for the first piece and $10 for each additional, up to twenty in total; diptychs and triptychs upload as a single image, and a portion of the entry-fee proceeds is donated to arts organisations. — Deadline: January 8, 2027. Fee: $25 + $10 each additional. Prize: $750 + 2×$250.

item.title: FRAME/SEQUENCE Issue 4 — On the Destruction of Art
item.description: FRAME/SEQUENCE is a Philadelphia print periodical founded in 2025 by photographer and educator Lily Colman (RISD MFA, 2020) as a publishing non-profit under the fiscal sponsorship of CultureWorks of Philadelphia, spotlighting underrepresented and emerging photographers, writers, artists and communities across Philadelphia and Greater Pennsylvania. Issue 4, due out as the March 2027 periodical, takes the theme "On the Destruction of Art": what it means to make work in an age of cultural and societal destruction, how artists keep working in those conditions, and how a society responds when art itself is debased, degraded or commodified. The editors want work that uses destruction or ephemerality as method — rupture and renewal — alongside writing that reads art's place in culture through an art-historical or contemporary lens, and they say explicitly that they are looking for everything from photographers working on the ground in real time to more interpretive photographic and written responses. The regional frame is relaxed for this issue: the periodical still focuses on Philadelphia, but submissions for Issue 4 are open to any artist or writer, and former University of the Arts students forced to transfer when that school closed, along with their professors, are especially encouraged. Photography, creative writing (poetry, fiction, creative nonfiction), visual art, mixed media and community-focused projects are accepted, and all visual art must incorporate photography in some way. Submit between five and ten images per edition as JPEG or PNG through the Airtable form, each file under 10 MB, 240 dpi acceptable and 300 dpi preferred for print; previously published work is eligible as long as you retain the right to republish, noted in the submission. There is no submission fee: the FAQ on the Issue 4 call page states "There is no submission fee. FRAME/SEQUENCE believes in removing financial barriers to participation in the arts community." Accepted contributors are paid a one-time cash award per accepted piece plus a royalty apportioned by level of contribution out of a shared royalty pool paid through the fiscal sponsor; artists keep full ownership and all rights and may keep using, selling or publishing the work, signing a publishing agreement by DocuSign if selected. Three inconsistencies sit on the organiser's own pages, and one of them is about money. The submissions FAQ still answers the deadline question with the inaugural issue's window (June 20 – July 18, 2025), while the dated Issue 4 block on both the submissions page and the homepage reads September 15 – November 15, 2026. The About page says twice that the periodical charges nothing to submit — "we do not charge a submission fee, and we pay our artists for having their work published" and "submissions are always free" — the live Issue 4 Airtable form carries no payment step, no fee line and no membership question, and as of 13 October 2026 the call page's own FAQ agrees: "There is no submission fee." And the team page calls the periodical quarterly where the homepage and submissions page call it semiannual. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + cash award per accepted piece.

item.title: Collected Light · Photosynthesis NZ
item.description: Open call for "all art made with light" from Photosynthesis, a fully volunteer-run non-profit in Ōtautahi Christchurch that operates the only gallery in the city dedicated to photography, alongside a community darkroom, studio and digital workspaces for hire. Collected Light is the second edition of a regular mega group show: the first, Open 2026, ran in February and March 2026 with more than 80 artists and over 180 pieces, and the organisers describe the format as "a cross-section of the state-of-our-arts". Artists of all ages and experience levels may enter one to three still works made with light — photographs, prints, photo books and zines are all named. Each entry needs a title, a short description, an image and a display plan. There is no size limit, but you must give the finished outside height and width in millimetres including any frame or mount (and the depth if it matters), measured as planned if the work is not yet printed; later changes need the gallery's approval so it can plan the layout. A panel reviews every entry after submissions close and selects the show; the organisers say they cannot include every entry but hope to include at least one submission per artist. Work may be offered for sale with a koha commission of 20% to Photosynthesis on any sale. Print workshops run through November for anyone who needs help producing their piece. Installation begins 28 November and the show opens on 4 December 2026 at the Photosynthesis gallery on Battersea Street in Sydenham; the call page says the exhibition end date is still to be confirmed, but the gallery’s own exhibitions calendar already dates the run 4–20 December 2026. Selection, delivery and collection dates and the opening time are still to be announced. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Pedantic Arts Residency 2027
item.description: Four-week residency on Penn Avenue in Pittsburgh's Garfield arts corridor, run by Pedantic Arts (a Casey Droege Cultural Productions programme now becoming a standalone non-profit). Each cohort is three creatives in three distinct roles — a visual artist, an organiser/curator and a writer — and the programme is built around exchange and study rather than output: it asks for no final deliverable and states that it "prioritizes immersion over production". The visual-artist role is defined broadly as "anyone working in a creative field of the Fine Arts be it painting, craft, performance art, social practice, etc." The call names no medium at all, but Pedantic’s own cohort archive does: its June 2023 cohort page describes that cohort’s visual artist, Akea Brionne, as "a Creole visual artist based in Detroit, MI whose work sits at the intersection of photography, textiles, and moving image", and carries Cranbrook’s May 2026 announcement of her first solo museum exhibition under the headline "Photography Alumna Akea Brionne". Residents get a private bedroom and desk in a newly built three-bedroom apartment (shared kitchen, living space, laundry, outdoor space and street parking; one bedroom and bathroom are ADA-compliant and the building has a lift), a $2,000 stipend paid half on arrival and half on completion, facilitated access to Pittsburgh's creative community, tickets and passes to local institutions, and a Pittsburgh-based guide working in a similar field who builds a schedule and opens up local contacts. Weekly programming includes private dinners, studio visits and museum tours, some public and some reserved for the cohort. Two terms are on offer in this call: Summer 2027, 5 June – 2 July 2027, and Fall 2027, 2 – 29 October 2027; you may apply for both but will be invited to only one. Applicants must be 18 or older and must live outside the greater Pittsburgh metropolitan area, which Pedantic defines as Allegheny, Armstrong, Beaver, Butler, Fayette, Washington and Westmoreland counties — Pittsburgh-based creatives are pointed to the Get Involved form instead. International applicants are welcome and Pedantic says it will support visa applications, while cautioning prospective residents to check their own country's travel position first; residents arrange and pay for their own travel to Pittsburgh. Applications were free through 28 September 2026 and cost $20 from 29 September, payable to Casey Droege Cultural Productions, until the open call closes on 15 October 2026 at 11:59pm EST. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: 4-week residency + $2,000 stipend.

item.title: I would like it to be · Grosse Pointe Artists Association
item.description: A juried show at the Grosse Pointe Artists Association's gallery on the War Memorial campus in Grosse Pointe Farms, on the Lake St Clair shore north-east of Detroit. The theme asks artists to share a dream or creative spark — to picture the world ahead for themselves and for others as they would like it to be. The juror is Sabrina Nelson, a Detroit artist of more than thirty-five years and a Kresge Artist Fellow, who teaches studio art at the Detroit Institute of Arts, where she lectures and gives artist demonstrations, and is on staff at the College for Creative Studies. First prize is a solo show at the gallery in 2027. The call is open to any artist over 18, plus alumni of the association's Promising Artists exhibitions — there is no geographic bar, but accepted work has to be in the gallery's hands for intake between noon and 2.30pm on Saturday 5 December, so travel or shipping arrangements are the artist's problem to solve. Work must be original: anything made under an instructor's direction, commercial kits, prefabricated models and hobby crafts are all ineligible, as are large installations and pieces already shown with the association. There is no size limit, though gallery space is a factor in final acceptance. Entry runs $30 for members and $40 for non-members for the first two pieces, with up to four more at $10 each and a $3 transaction fee on top; images must be JPGs of at least 600 × 600 pixels, evenly lit and free of reflections. Two-dimensional work should arrive framed and ready to hang, with acrylic rather than glass. Not everything has to be priced to sell, but anything that is and does carries a commission of 35% on member work and 45% on non-member work, so price accordingly. Entries close at midnight on Monday 16 November 2026, results are emailed by Friday 20 November, the exhibition runs 9 December 2026 to 22 January 2027 with a gallery talk at 2pm on Saturday 12 December, and work is collected between 10am and noon on Saturday 23 January. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $40 for 2 works ($30 members), $10 per extra work, +$3 transaction fee. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Flower & Fauna: A Botanical & Beings Exhibition · Avondale Arts Alliance
item.description: A themed winter show at the Avondale Arts Center, the volunteer-run gallery of the Avondale Arts Alliance just east of Atlanta in Avondale Estates. Every work must feature flowers, plants, animals or some combination of the three — the alliance states that anything outside that is disqualified automatically — and both traditional treatments and loose, creative interpretations are invited, with no restriction on medium beyond the subject rule. Entrants may submit one to six pieces in a single entry, one entry per artist, as JPG, PDF or PNG files up to 50MB each; the fee is $15 for three pieces and $30 for six, artists 18 and under enter free with a voucher code, and the alliance asks anyone for whom the fee is a hardship to email before submitting. The call is open only to artists in Atlanta and the surrounding area, because accepted work has to be hand delivered: drop-off is 10am to 2pm on Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November, the gallery does not accept shipped artwork, and a friend or family member may deliver on an artist's behalf. Status emails go out by midnight on Saturday 31 October. The exhibition opens with a 6–9pm reception on Saturday 14 November and closes with another on Saturday 19 December; attendance at neither is required. All work must be priced for sale with the alliance retaining 30% of any sale, and prices cannot be changed after acceptance, so the alliance asks artists to build the commission into the price before applying. Submissions close at 11.59pm on Friday 23 October 2026. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $15 for 3 works, $30 for 6. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals 2027–2028 · Alexander Brest Gallery
item.description: The Alexander Brest Gallery is the exhibition space of the Linda Berry Stein College of Arts & Sciences at Jacksonville University, on the university's riverfront campus across the St Johns River from downtown Jacksonville, and it programmes its season from an annual open call rather than from invitations alone. For the 2027–2028 season the gallery, under director Zakriya Rabani, is taking proposals for its 2,300 square foot space in 2D, 3D, installation and video work — photography sits inside the 2D remit, and the call is explicit that proposals are welcome from established and emerging artists in all mediums. Both solo and group exhibitions are considered, as are curatorial proposals, and a team may apply with one shared résumé of no more than a page per member. Applications are free and go in as a single PDF of no more than 50MB, named LastName_FirstName_ExhibitionTitle_Proposal.pdf, holding three things: an exhibition narrative that opens with a clear thesis statement (project proposals for unfinished or installation work also need a timeline, and any on-site making has to be installable in under three days); a CV of one to two pages per person with a preferred contact method; and an image list of up to 12 high-resolution images for a solo show or three per person for a group show, each image on its own page at large size with artist, title, medium, dimensions and year underneath. Video and audio work is submitted as streaming links plus stills, and an all-video application needs no image PDF at all. One requirement sets this call apart from a straight exhibition application: every proposal must include a student engagement activity at JU — a studio visit, a lecture, a tool or material demonstration, student participation in the exhibition narrative, or a collaboration with another college on campus. The gallery publishes its floor plan and installation photographs for applicants to plan against, and states that it is committed to showing artists across race, colour, creed, gender, gender variance, sexual orientation, national origin, age, religion, marital status, political affiliation and mental or physical disability. The call is open to artists anywhere in the continental United States and closes on 14 December 2026. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: NYC Open Call 2027–28 · apexart
item.description: apexart, the non-profit at 291 Church Street in Tribeca, runs its New York open call every October, and this round is for the 2027–28 exhibition season.
